## CONVERGING target contract — implementation alignment pending

This document is the single target authority for the reopened structured
authoring API, its Plan-identity integration, and certified authoring/compiled
diagrams. Runtime alignment to the target API remains pending; the target is
not accepted or stabilized, and its examples are not yet executable.

The existing runtime remains the frozen implementation baseline until target
alignment. Accepted numerical operations, physical component models, units,
workspace evidence, and Result meanings remain authoritative and are not
redefined here. No compatibility path from the frozen flat-node or
catalog-hint candidates is promised.
:::

## Product promise

An author declares each physical component, electrical connection, ownership
boundary, and structural role once. Numerical compilation and diagram
projection consume that same declaration:

```text
Library component facts
          |
          v
CircuitPlan + inline SubsystemPlan + reusable CompositePlan
          |
          +----> numerical lowering and existing Run/Result evidence
          |
          +----> authoring or compiled certified diagram
```

The diagram never supplies topology to the solver. The solver never infers
authoring intent from component names, a drawing, or incidental graph shape.

This contract owns:

- the structured electrical grammar shared by root, inline, and reusable
  scopes;
- its ownership and public-handle boundaries;
- diagram-only layout hints over authored handles;
- authoring and compiled projection evidence;
- Plan, structural, connectivity, presentation, and compiler identity
  boundaries; and
- authoring, layout, and audit failure behavior.

The [Component Authoring Contract](../component-authoring.qmd) retains physical
factory values, component schemas, RLGC, Josephson, SQUID, mutual-inductance,
and backend-realization authority. The
[V1 Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd) retains execution, view,
request, workspace, Result, and report authority.

## One authority and three assembly scopes {#one-authority-three-scopes}

`CircuitPlan` remains the sole root physical authority. Two child-scope forms
use the same grammar without becoming alternate Plans:

| Scope | Creation | Ownership boundary | Product result |
|---|---|---|---|
| root `CircuitPlan` | `CircuitPlan(id=...)` | complete circuit, Ports, and Run input | one sealable Plan |
| inline `SubsystemPlan` | `scope.subsystem(id=...)` | Plan-owned hierarchy used in this declaration | attached mutable child sealed by its parent |
| Library `CompositePlan` | `CompositePlan(id=id, library=self)` | factory-owned reusable hierarchy | one immutable `ComponentInstance` from `.build()` |

`SubsystemPlan` has no detached constructor or `.build()` path. It is always
created by and attached to its parent. An author may nest inline Subsystems
recursively. A Subsystem is an explicit ownership declaration; SCNSim never
infers one from values, topology, names, modes, geometry, or intended research
use.

A `CompositePlan` is detached only while a Library factory authors it. Its
internal native leaves retain their exact catalog provenance, and `.build()`
publishes only the declared pins, parameters, coordinates, and inductive
branches. A consumer cannot reach through the resulting component to hidden
children.

## Common structured-authoring grammar {#structured-authoring-grammar}

The operations below have one target spelling on `CircuitPlan`,
`SubsystemPlan`, and `CompositePlan`, except where the signatures name a
narrower owner. `AssemblyScope`, `PublicBoundaryScope`, `StructuredEndpoint`,
`LinkEndpoint`, and `ElementUse` are documentation unions, not additional
constructible classes. A `*` marks the keyword-only boundary:

```text
AssemblyScope := CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan | CompositePlan
PublicBoundaryScope := SubsystemPlan | CompositePlan
StructuredEndpoint := BusRef | TapRef | PinRef | GroundRef
LinkEndpoint := BusRef | TapRef | PinRef
ElementUse := ComponentInstance | TwoTerminalUse

AssemblyScope.add(component: ComponentInstance) -> ComponentInstance
AssemblyScope.subsystem(*, id: str) -> SubsystemPlan
AssemblyScope.bus(*, id: str | None = None) -> BusRef
BusRef.tap(*, id: str) -> TapRef
AssemblyScope.series(
    *, id: str, start: StructuredEndpoint,
    elements: tuple[ElementUse, ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> SeriesRef
AssemblyScope.parallel(
    *, id: str, start: StructuredEndpoint,
    branches: tuple[tuple[ElementUse, ...], ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> ParallelRef
AssemblyScope.branch(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
    elements: tuple[ElementUse, ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> BranchRef
AssemblyScope.link(
    *, id: str, endpoints: tuple[LinkEndpoint, ...],
) -> LinkRef
AssemblyScope.ground_pins(*, pins: tuple[PinRef, ...]) -> None
AssemblyScope.couple_inductive(
    *, id: str, inductor_a: InductiveBranchRef,
    inductor_b: InductiveBranchRef,
    coupling_coefficient: Quantity,
) -> CouplingRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_pin(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
) -> PinRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_coordinate(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
) -> CoordinateRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_inductive_branch(
    *, id: str, branch: InductiveBranchRef,
) -> InductiveBranchRef
CompositePlan.expose_parameter(
    *, id: str, parameter: ParameterRef,
) -> ParameterRef
ComponentInstance.between(
    pin_1: PinRef, pin_2: PinRef,
) -> TwoTerminalUse
CircuitPlan.add_port(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
    role: Literal["terminated", "nonloading_probe"],
    reference_impedance: Quantity,
) -> PortRef
```

IDs are typed and scoped. Added components and inline Subsystems share the
direct-part namespace of their parent. Buses have another namespace, while
series, parallel, branch, link, and coupling declarations share the structure
namespace. Public pins, coordinates, and inductive branches each have separate
exposure namespaces. Ports have a root-only namespace, and tap IDs are unique
within one bus. Those structural-handle identities include occurrence path,
kind, and local ID, so the same spelling may validly name a bus and its public
pin or a bus and its Port. An exposed parameter retains its independent
definitions-collection/local-ID identity. Compiler-assigned anonymous/internal
keys cannot collide with user IDs.

Returned refs are typed, immutable authoring handles; raw strings and foreign
handles do not substitute for them. `ground_pins()` has no ID and returns no
public handle: its call grouping is source provenance, not another structure or
ground domain.

### Register a body, bind its terminals, then choose its structural role

`scope.add(component)` registers one catalog-created body. Registration alone
does not connect it. Terminal completeness and structural use are separate
checks. Before complete-graph preflight, every required terminal must be bound.
An ordinary two-terminal native body must also belong to exactly one
`series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` declaration.

An ordinary factory component with exactly two declared pins is itself an
`ElementUse`; its factory-defined terminal order supplies orientation:

```python
capacitor = scope.add(
    components.capacitor(id="coupler", capacitance=6.0 * u.fF)
)
coupling = scope.series(
    id="coupling",
    start=input_bus,
    elements=(capacitor,),
    end=output_bus,
)
```

An already complete Composite occurrence or native multi-terminal body may
instead remain one independent direct peer of its scope when every required
pin is explicitly bound. If its terminal schema permits structural use, the
author may consume the whole body in exactly one structure. A grounded
Composite with one public signal pin is already structurally complete because
its internal native leaves are assembled; after that public pin is bound, the
occurrence may remain an independent peer.

For one structural use of a complete multi-terminal body,
`component.between(pin_1, pin_2)` supplies the ordered endpoint pair. It is
optional when that body remains an independent peer and never selects a
preferred physical conductor or numerical priority. Every remaining pin must
still be bound. The body appears once; another pair cannot clone it. CPW and
MTL components retain one ordered multi-terminal electrical model and never
become scalar-equivalent shortcuts.

`series()` and `.between()` state endpoint incidence and authored order. They
do not assert a scalar two-terminal equivalent or equal current through a body
whose complete model includes internal reference shunts. An IDC therefore
retains all three capacitance branches, and CPW/MTL bodies retain complete RLGC
matrices, conductor order, and every remaining terminal binding.

Registration, binding, and structure therefore cannot manufacture a phantom
component, duplicate one body, hide an electrical shortcut, or infer an
engineering group. Two electrically equivalent declarations may retain
different authored structure and therefore need not share Plan or semantic
identity.

Repeated contact with a public terminal is allowed only on its already
declared net. It does not duplicate the native body or let one terminal join
two nets.

### Endpoints, buses, taps, and ground {#buses-taps-and-ground}

Structured operators accept these endpoint types where their signatures allow:

```text
BusRef | TapRef | PinRef | GroundRef
```

A `CoordinateRef` is an analysis selector, not a wiring endpoint. An endpoint
must belong to the current scope or be a public pin of one immediate child.
Hidden child refs, foreign refs, implicit loads, implicit grounding, and
hidden zero-ohm elements fail before Plan seal.

These handles answer different questions:

| Handle | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BusRef` | one authored electrical net inside its owning scope |
| `TapRef` | one explicitly named attachment site on that same bus |
| `PinRef` | a component terminal or a child-scope boundary exposed to its parent |
| `CoordinateRef` | a selector that makes an electrical coordinate available to analysis |

Ordinary wiring may use a `BusRef` directly. A named tap is useful only when
the author needs to identify one attachment independently—for example, to
constrain the presentation order of several contacts on one bus. A tap does
not create another net, and its ID or declaration order is not a layout
instruction. Likewise, a public pin whose ID is `"tap"` remains a `PinRef`;
its spelling does not make it a `TapRef`.

`scope.bus(id=None)` declares one logical net. A named root bus publishes an
`ElectricNodeRef` immediately through `.node`. An anonymous root bus becomes
public only when `add_port()` promotes it to the Port-named coordinate;
accessing `.node` before that declaration fails. A private child bus does not
publish a root coordinate; its owner must use `expose_coordinate()`. Taps
delegate `.node` to their bus and therefore resolve the same eventual
`ElectricNodeRef`, while their attachment handles and drawing anchors remain
distinct. Promotion is an authoring declaration, not a render side effect, and
Plan sealing preserves the handle's resolved meaning. A tap has no coordinate
argument.

`scope.ground` is the `GroundRef` for the single canonical Plan reference. It
is valid only where `series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` accepts a structured
endpoint. It is not a catalog component, another physical ground model, a
`link()` endpoint, or a page-wide drawing rail. Ground glyphs remain local to
the declarations that establish their role.

### Series, parallel, branch, link, and grounding {#structured-operators}

`series()`, `parallel()`, and `branch()` are component-containing assembly
declarations: each establishes real electrical incidence and a readable
authored role. They are not labels applied after arbitrary wiring. By contrast,
`link()` joins existing endpoints directly and contains no component.

`series()` requires at least one `ElementUse`. Electrical order is the tuple
order, and each adjacent pair creates one generated private internal node. A
one-element coupling capacitor is valid. Its start and end cannot silently be
the same endpoint; an intended cycle requires distinct declared junctions and
another explicit path.

When an author needs a public midpoint in a series chain, the midpoint must be
declared first as a bus and the chain split into two structures at that bus.
Compiler-generated private intermediate nodes are not addressable pins or taps.

`parallel()` requires at least two nonempty ordered element tuples. Every
branch shares exactly the same start/end pair and owns distinct internal nodes.
Empty tuples do not mean a short. The returned `.branches` is the immutable
tuple of generated `SeriesRef` handles. Each branch's series order is an
electrical fact; the branch collection itself is electrically unordered.
Declaration order supplies default visual order and may enter authoring
provenance, but a graphical permutation does not change branch membership or
the circuit.

`branch()` uses the same nonempty chain semantics, but `at` must be a declared
`BusRef` or `TapRef`. It states that the chain departs a through-bus without
severing it. This side-branch role enters semantic identity and is not inferred
from the part name or final drawing. A branch may have the same electrical
incidence as a series declaration from that bus; it additionally records the
side-branch role, never current direction. A grounded branch prefers an
outward/down orientation when feasible, but the drawing preference does not
change its electrical meaning.

`link()` declares one direct conductive relation with no component. Its
`endpoints` tuple contains at least two `BusRef`, `TapRef`, or `PinRef` handles;
tuple order conveys neither direction nor layout, and canonical membership uses
the existing typed scoped identities. One N-endpoint link is one authored
zero-wire relation, not a star of invented center branches or a pairwise
clique. It adds and moves no component, consumes no registered body, and cannot
replace a required `series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` declaration. There is
no `start=`/`end=` compatibility spelling for the target link API.

A parent may link its own endpoints and public pins of its immediate children.
It may not use a child's private bus or tap, even when a Python variable still
holds that handle. A link can make a parent bus, an exposed child pin, and the
pin's backing private bus one final voltage node without erasing any
owner-local identity. A parent bus is optional when a physical structure can
terminate directly at the public pin.

`link()` rejects a raw `GroundRef`; external grounding has the dedicated
`ground_pins()` operation below. It also rejects an endpoint already equivalent
to ground before that call, duplicate logical endpoints, or a no-op whose every
endpoint already belongs to one pre-call electrical class. Partial overlap is
legal when the declaration safely joins at least two pre-call classes and
reuses existing wire geometry rather than duplicating it. Separate links may
therefore extend one net over time without restating earlier wires.

For ordinary non-ground connection, a link may not merge distinct `BusRef`s
owned by its invoking scope, whether those buses are named or anonymous. A
child's private backing bus does not count as another parent-owned bus. The same
rule detects direct, pin-mediated, tap-mediated, and transitive attempts,
including a later edit inside an inline child that would create a conflict in
the containing Plan. It does not ban legitimate public return pins merely
because their component has more than one terminal.

`ground_pins(pins=(...))` accepts one or more eligible `PinRef`s in the current
scope or on immediate children. It grounds each pin's entire currently
connected net, so one call may explicitly ground several otherwise independent
return nets. Distinct pins on the same previously ungrounded net are valid.
Duplicate logical pins or any pin already equivalent to ground reject the whole
call; no subset is silently accepted. The tuple order and batch boundary are
provenance only and define neither geometry nor separate ground domains.

Connectivity validation uses one zero-wire equivalence relation for buses and
taps, public exposures, links, canonical ground, and structured wire endpoint
incidences. It never unions through an R, L, C, JJ, or transmission-line body,
nor infers a short from a numerical value. Coincident structured endpoints,
model-specific terminal shorts, one-Port-per-final-node, grounded Ports, public
pin membership, and complete child invariants are checked over the affected
enclosing Plan.

Each authoring operation prepares and validates its complete effect before an
atomic commit. A rejection preserves IDs, structures, aliases, body
consumption, public exposures, parameter definitions, revision/cache state,
and the diagnostic source paths of successfully committed declarations; it
adds no diagnostic or provenance history for the rejected attempt. A rejected
structure ID is reusable. A link that was legal when declared may later become
grounded by `ground_pins()` or a structured ground endpoint without being
retroactively reclassified as an invalid historical link.

Incomplete authoring remains legal while the graph is editable.
`CompositePlan.build()`, immutable render capture, and `CircuitRun` sealing
perform complete validation over their ownership boundary. A failed authoring
check leaves that state editable and unsealed; rendering does not seal it.
Atomicity covers SCNSim's authoring state, not arbitrary side effects inside a
user's Python factory. A well-typed ownership, cardinality, stale-ref, or
connectivity violation reports `SCNSimValidationError(stage="authoring")` with
the conflicting endpoints, scope, buses, and earlier path. Wrong endpoint or
container types raise `TypeError`; post-seal mutation raises `PlanSealedError`.

Real graph cycles remain valid when authored as separate junctions and
physical paths.

The target decision boundary is therefore exact:

| Declaration | Outcome |
|---|---|
| one bus plus two immediate-child public pins in one link | one valid N-endpoint zero-wire relation |
| two or more pre-call classes with one already-overlapping endpoint | valid extension when every other invariant holds |
| duplicate logical endpoint, or all endpoints already one class | reject as duplicate or redundant |
| two distinct buses owned by the invoking scope, directly or through pins/taps | reject the complete operation |
| a private child ref, foreign/stale ref, raw ground, Port, coordinate, string, or wrong container | reject without publishing a declaration |
| distinct public return pins, including two already on one ungrounded net, passed to `ground_pins()` | valid explicit grounding when the component and Port invariants hold |
| duplicate or already-grounded pin in a `ground_pins()` batch | reject the complete batch |
| connection that shorts a physical element's endpoints or grounds a Port node | reject the complete operation |

No numerical near-zero rule participates in this matrix. Wires establish
equivalence; physical bodies do not.

### Three local-ground roles {#local-ground-roles}

The target distinguishes three authored responsibilities:

1. **Intrinsic ground.** A subsystem connects a real `series()`, `parallel()`,
   or `branch()` endpoint to its own `scope.ground`. The subsystem itself owns
   that grounding and exposes only the boundaries its parent needs.
2. **Parent-applied ground.** An otherwise ungrounded module exposes an
   ordinary return bus as a public pin. Its parent calls `ground_pins()` on
   that pin. A bus whose ID contains `ground` remains ordinary until this
   explicit operation.
3. **Port load/reference.** `add_port()` supplies its declared load to the
   canonical reference. A Port has no separately wireable ground pin, and its
   graphical ground anchor is not a public electrical handle.

The parent-applied form is deliberately small:

```python
return_pin = child.expose_pin(id="return", at=return_bus)
plan.ground_pins(pins=(return_pin,))
```

All three resolve to the same canonical reference for numerical lowering. The
authoring projection nevertheless preserves the intrinsic branch, the
parent-side ground attachment outside the child boundary, or the Port load at
its authored locality. Several local glyphs therefore do not imply several
electrical grounds, while one multi-pin grounding call does not force a shared
cross-subsystem ground rail.

Every final non-ground alias denotes one solver degree of freedom. Ground
aliases provide no selectable non-reference analytical coordinate. Linking or
grounding creates no implicit `NetworkViewRef`, transform, retained boundary,
or reduction.

### Canonical-ground visual grammar {#native-branches-and-ground}

Native R/L/C/JJ branches are visible electrical symbols. A local ground branch
terminates in a ground glyph near its owning scope. Several glyphs may denote
the same canonical reference; their placement or call grouping does not create
distinct electrical grounds. N-link geometry is shared and drawn once rather
than as duplicate pairwise wires. A continuous bus or link is conductive.
Ownership regions, labels, guides, and provenance panels are nonconductive and
must not look like wires or junction dots.

Only transmission-line and multi-conductor-line bodies may use an electrical
box with a complete pin/conductor legend. Ordinary C/L/JJ networks remain
expanded native symbols; a Subsystem box never hides their topology.

## Public boundaries and parameters {#public-boundaries}

Inline and reusable scopes deliberately publish their consumer surface:

```python
terminal = child.expose_pin(id="terminal", at=terminal_bus)
mode = child.expose_coordinate(id="mode", at=terminal_bus)
coil = child.expose_inductive_branch(id="coil", branch=inductor_branch)
```

- `expose_pin()` returns a public wiring `PinRef` for the parent.
- `expose_coordinate()` returns a public analysis `CoordinateRef`.
- `expose_inductive_branch()` returns an oriented branch eligible for explicit
  mutual coupling.

One internal node exposes at most one public pin. Its bus may still have
several taps. A private named bus is not automatically a root coordinate;
coordinate exposure is explicit. The `.pin(name)`, `.coordinate(name)`, and
`.inductive_branch(name)` accessors return only declared public handles.
Externally commoning two distinct public return pins does not rewrite that
immutable child schema or imply the pins were intrinsically shorted. Distinct
pins on one child are not rejected merely for sharing the external reference;
complete internal topology and model-specific terminal constraints decide
whether that commoning is physically valid.

Parameter definitions are independent of assembly ownership. A scope acquires
a parameter only when a registered physical component field consumes the ref.
A reusable Composite may then publish that already-bound ref:

```python
public_capacitance = composite.expose_parameter(
    id="capacitance", parameter=capacitance
)
```

The built component's `parameter(name)` lookup returns the original public ref;
it does not create a definition or mutate its baseline. Compatible factory
slots accept either a fixed `Quantity` or a compatible independent
`ParameterRef`. Adding the part records the real field binding and any declared
fan-out. Parameters are never decorative same-value labels disconnected from
physical leaves, and a parent never selects a hidden child parameter by path
guessing. The [Parameter System contract](parameter-system.qmd) owns
definition identity, Plan adoption, values, spaces, and operation binding.

## Logical Ports remain root-owned {#root-owned-ports}

Only `CircuitPlan` creates logical Ports:

```python
signal_port = plan.add_port(
    id="signal_in",
    at=signal_bus,
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
```

`at` is a root `BusRef` or `TapRef`. The Port binds the existing raw-network
load exactly once and returns a `PortRef` for Direct, HB, and view selection.
`role` remains exactly `"terminated"` or `"nonloading_probe"`; the latter is
eligible for the accepted PTC operation but is not portrayed as already
compensated. Final electrical identity is resolved through buses, taps, public
child exposures, and anonymous-bus promotion: one resulting electric node may
own at most one logical Port even when several handles alias that node. Inline
Subsystems and Library Composites cannot create Ports.

## Inductive coupling remains explicit and nonconductive {#inductive-coupling}

`couple_inductive()` consumes two eligible oriented `InductiveBranchRef`s and
one signed dimensionless coupling coefficient:

```python
mutual = plan.couple_inductive(
    id="mutual",
    inductor_a=left.inductive_branch("coil"),
    inductor_b=right.inductive_branch("coil"),
    coupling_coefficient=-0.12 * u.dimensionless,
)
```

It adds no conductive edge. Branch orientation owns the sign; SCNSim does not
infer it from symbol placement. Existing realizability, reciprocity, and
positive-definite inductance checks remain the physical authority.

## Complete structural examples {#structured-examples}

### Grounded LC and reusable resonator

Chapter 1 begins with the minimal inline example: one signal bus and two native elements
form an explicit `parallel()` between that bus and `scope.ground`. The scope
binds literal C/L values and exposes only its terminal. The parent joins that
pin to a named root bus through `link(endpoints=(...))`, places a 6 fF
capacitor in
`series()`, and adds one terminated Port. Chapters 2–3 repeat the same
fixed-value declaration. Chapter 4 independently defines C/L inputs and binds
them through actual component fields; Chapter 5 selects ordered points. This
does not retroactively make every fixed component value a parameter.

Chapters 8–10 repeat the same internal grammar in a Library `CompositePlan` and
then consume its one public terminal. The electrical values may match, but the
factory-owned version has different ownership and provenance. No Plan or
semantic digest equality is claimed across the two authoring sources.

### SQUID, cycles, and mutual coupling

A finite-loop two-junction SQUID uses one direct junction path and one ordered
loop-inductor/junction path. Each Josephson component owns its intrinsic
parallel `Cj` exactly once; an exact zero omits that leaf. The shared public
parameters below fan out to the two real junction bodies rather than acting as
decorative labels:

```python
from scnsim import (
    CircuitPlan,
    ParameterDefinitions,
    ParameterSpec,
    components,
    units as u,
)

inputs = ParameterDefinitions(id="finite_loop_inputs")
josephson_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="josephson_inductance",
    baseline=310.0 * u.pH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.pH),
)
junction_capacitance = inputs.parameter(
    id="junction_capacitance",
    baseline=2.0 * u.fF,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.fF),
)
loop_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="loop_inductance",
    baseline=45.0 * u.pH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.pH),
)
pump_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="pump_inductance",
    baseline=1.0 * u.nH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.nH),
)
plan = CircuitPlan(id="finite_loop_coupling")

squid = plan.subsystem(id="squid")
j1 = squid.add(
    components.josephson_junction(
        id="j1",
        josephson_inductance=josephson_inductance,
        junction_capacitance=junction_capacitance,
    )
)
j2 = squid.add(
    components.josephson_junction(
        id="j2",
        josephson_inductance=josephson_inductance,
        junction_capacitance=junction_capacitance,
    )
)
loop = squid.add(
    components.inductor(id="loop", inductance=loop_inductance)
)
a = squid.bus(id="a")
b = squid.bus(id="b")
squid.parallel(
    id="finite_loop",
    start=a,
    branches=((j1,), (loop, j2)),
    end=b,
)
squid.expose_pin(id="terminal_1", at=a)
squid.expose_pin(id="terminal_2", at=b)
squid.expose_inductive_branch(
    id="loop",
    branch=loop.inductive_branch("self"),
)

pump = plan.subsystem(id="pump")
pump_coil = pump.add(
    components.inductor(id="coil", inductance=pump_inductance)
)
pump_bus = pump.bus(id="terminal")
pump.branch(
    id="coil_to_ground",
    at=pump_bus,
    elements=(pump_coil,),
    end=pump.ground,
)
pump.expose_pin(id="terminal", at=pump_bus)
pump.expose_inductive_branch(
    id="coil",
    branch=pump_coil.inductive_branch("self"),
)

signal_bus = plan.bus(id="signal")
pump_drive_bus = plan.bus(id="pump_drive")
plan.link(
    id="squid_signal",
    endpoints=(signal_bus, squid.pin("terminal_1")),
)
plan.ground_pins(pins=(squid.pin("terminal_2"),))
plan.link(
    id="pump_terminal",
    endpoints=(pump_drive_bus, pump.pin("terminal")),
)
plan.couple_inductive(
    id="flux_pump",
    inductor_a=squid.inductive_branch("loop"),
    inductor_b=pump.inductive_branch("coil"),
    coupling_coefficient=0.12 * u.dimensionless,
)
```

The `parallel()` call creates the two genuine paths
`a -> J1 -> b` and `a -> L_loop -> J2 -> b`; it does not model two directly
parallel junctions with an unspecified loop. This is a real cycle through
distinct paths. The SQUID's exposed return is grounded by its parent rather
than rewritten as an intrinsic child ground. The outer pump scope is completely
connected before its oriented branch participates in the explicitly
nonconductive mutual relation.
The exact Josephson and DC-SQUID physics remain in the linked component and
Root Knowledge authorities; this contract chooses only structural expression
and does not substitute the negligible-loop effective-cosine model.

### Multi-terminal line

For an N-conductor transmission line, `reference_conductor` is RLGC metadata,
not a public `PinRef`. N=1 has two public signal pins; N>1 has exactly 2N
ordered public signal-conductor pins. One possible structural declaration uses
`.between(...)` to place one selected head/tail pair and binds every remaining
pin explicitly by `link(endpoints=(...))` or a bus. An independent line instead
binds every pin explicitly and omits `.between()`. Either form retains the body,
conductor order, matrix coefficients, and section provenance exactly once.

### Three-subsystem model

Chapters 13–16 author one `feedline`, one grounded `readout`, and one `floating`
inline Subsystem at the root. The feedline owns two independent N=1 line
sections and public input/tap/output pins. The floating scope owns one mutual
C/L parallel network plus two separate ground branches. Root capacitors join
feedline to readout and readout to each floating terminal. Root terminated and
nonloading-probe Ports retain their distinct roles.

The quarter-wave readout is explicitly a local lumped approximation, not a
claim of distributed equivalence. The tutorials contain public generic values
only and supply no scientific acceptance or consumer evidence.

## Plan identity and one-declaration lowering {#structured-plan-identity}

The target Plan snapshot preserves, at minimum:

- scoped IDs and recursive ownership;
- operator kind and endpoints;
- ordered series elements and parallel branches;
- bus/tap identities, N-endpoint link membership, public exposures, and final
  zero-wire equivalence;
- canonical-ground membership and parent-applied grounding locations;
- logical Ports and roles;
- component catalog source and parameters; and
- oriented coupling declarations.

Endpoint order within one fixed N-link is canonicalized and does not change
semantic membership. Replacing one N-link by several binary links may preserve
electrical equivalence, but it changes the authored structures and therefore
need not preserve Plan or semantic identities. The batch or tuple order of
`ground_pins()` does not change physical ground membership or diagram digests.

Numerical and diagram lowering consume that one snapshot. Pure
`SchematicLayout`, Theme, and final geometry remain outside Plan/request
identity. By contrast, declared ownership, order, branch roles, and exposures
are semantic structure. Rewriting a flat circuit into a hierarchy may preserve
electrical values/connectivity while changing Plan and semantic identities.

These structural declarations require a deliberately aligned successor Plan
schema and canonical encoder before the target can execute. The successor
encoding promises neither old/new Plan-SHA equality nor compatibility with the
frozen implementation; it does not create another public authoring API.
Factory-source changes may alter catalog/Plan provenance even when electrical
values are unchanged. Invariance applies only when catalog source and all
physical/structural declarations are fixed.

## Diagram request and layout hints {#schematic-layout}

The target keeps one diagram request:

```python
CircuitDiagramSpec(
    representation="authoring",
    theme=Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values=True,
    show_provenance=True,
    layout=None,
)
```

Its exact target signature and Plan operation are:

```text
CircuitDiagramSpec(
    *, representation: Literal["authoring", "compiled"] = "authoring",
    theme: Theme = Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values: bool = True,
    show_provenance: bool = True,
    layout: SchematicLayout | None = None,
) -> CircuitDiagramSpec
CircuitPlan.render_schematic(
    spec: CircuitDiagramSpec = CircuitDiagramSpec(),
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | None = None,
) -> CircuitDiagramResult
```

`representation` selects the original structured-authoring projection or the
compiler-expanded projection. It cannot select a reduced View, transformed
coordinate system, `ParameterSpace`, PTC result, or solver Result. The optional
single `ParameterSet` selects physical values for that projection; it is not a
View or an optimizer-candidate lookup.

### Directly constructible SchematicLayout

`SchematicLayout` is immutable and defensively copies five optional mappings.
The target type shape below is contract notation, not executable Python:

```text
SchematicLayout(
    *,
    axes: Mapping[
        CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan |
        SeriesRef | ParallelRef | BranchRef,
        DiagramAxis,
    ] = {},
    order: Mapping[
        CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan | ParallelRef,
        tuple[ComponentInstance | SubsystemPlan | SeriesRef, ...],
    ] = {},
    terminal_sides: Mapping[PinRef | TapRef, DiagramSide] = {},
    port_sides: Mapping[PortRef, DiagramSide] = {},
    tap_order: Mapping[BusRef, tuple[TapRef, ...]] = {},
) -> SchematicLayout
```

`DiagramAxis` accepts only `HORIZONTAL` or `VERTICAL`; `DiagramSide` accepts
only `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TOP`, or `BOTTOM`. Both are strict string Enums and raw
strings raise `TypeError`.

- `axes` orients the rendered root `CircuitPlan`, an attached live inline
  `SubsystemPlan`, or a structured group. Rendering belongs only to
  `CircuitPlan`; a detached `CompositePlan` and private scopes inside a built
  Composite are not layout keys.
- For a scope key, `order` is a complete permutation of its direct peer
  `ComponentInstance` and `SubsystemPlan` handles. This includes a complete
  Composite occurrence or native multi-terminal body that remains independent.
  A component body already consumed by a series, parallel, or branch structure
  is not a peer; neither are buses, taps, Ports, or connector structures. The
  value must list every eligible peer exactly once—omission is a validation
  failure, not a partial hint. For a `ParallelRef` key, the value is exactly a
  complete permutation of its `.branches` `SeriesRef`s. Key-dependent
  validation rejects every other mixture. Electrical members inside a
  `SeriesRef` cannot be reordered.
- `terminal_sides` constrains public boundary pins or declared bus taps owned
  by the referenced scope.
- `port_sides` constrains root `PortRef`s.
- `tap_order` gives the relative geometric order of explicitly named taps on
  one authored bus. A key is a live root or inline-Subsystem `BusRef` in the
  rendered Plan, including an electrically private bus in either eligible
  scope. Layout-key eligibility does not publish electrical or analytical
  access. Its value is a complete permutation of that exact bus's declared
  `TapRef`s; an empty tuple is harmless only when the bus has no declared taps.
  Private buses inside a built Composite remain inaccessible.

`tap_order` binds the exact authored `BusRef` and its owner-region segment, not
canonical electrical-node identity. Parent and child buses joined by a public
pin therefore keep separate local order frames. Along the bus owner's effective
local axis, the listed named taps have strictly increasing projected
contact-anchor positions: left to right for `HORIZONTAL` and top to bottom for
`VERTICAL`. Axes on incident `SeriesRef`, `ParallelRef`, or `BranchRef` objects
do not redefine that frame. Implicit direct-bus contacts are renderer
bookkeeping, not public refs, and may automatically precede, interleave with,
or follow the named taps. The complete tuple orders only the named taps
relative to one another.

The mapping does not define current flow, series order, node order, a new tap,
or a connection. Default tap placement follows connected structure and other
eligible layout constraints; `.tap()` call order and words such as `left` or
`right` do not command geometry. Side constraints and `tap_order` are
conjoined; neither silently overrides the other. A raw string or any other
wrong key or value type raises `TypeError`. A well-typed stale, foreign, or
hidden bus or tap, a missing, duplicate, or other-bus tap, an incomplete
permutation, or an incompatible or otherwise conflicting hint raises
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_layout")`. Both failure classes reject
the request before a Result, workspace, or partial image exists.

Changing only `tap_order`, another layout mapping, or Theme preserves Plan,
connectivity, and semantic digests. Adding or removing an authored tap changes
the structural declaration and need not preserve Plan or semantic identity,
even when the electrical net is equivalent. A/B correspondence checks the bus
and tap facts; separate layout validation checks that the rendered geometry
obeys the hint.

Foreign, hidden, dead, duplicate, missing, or conflicting handles fail closed.
The refs bind live authoring ownership captured at render. Editing a mutable
unsealed Plan and rendering again captures the new declaration; there is no
pre-render catalog, public ref constructor, stale snapshot ceremony, or raw
coordinate override.

### Automatic layout and ownership regions

Without hints, local renderer rules follow explicit `series`, `parallel`,
`branch`, `bus`, `tap`, coupling, and scope ownership. They do not reconstruct
S/P/M neighbors, choose a global physical flow, or infer intent from names and
Port roles.

The default reading grammar is local and mechanical. Direct scope peers follow
author declaration order on a horizontal axis. A series reads start-to-end on
a horizontal axis. Each parallel branch also runs horizontally start-to-end,
and the branches stack top-to-bottom in declaration order. A `VERTICAL` axis
hint rotates the whole parallel group: branches then run top-to-bottom and
stack left-to-right. Grounded ends and glyphs prefer below their local block,
and a branch departs its declared through-bus toward its endpoint block. A hint
never reverses electrical pins or series order. Source order is a reading
convention, never inferred physical signal, energy, or current flow.

Each Subsystem is recursively expanded into native child structure inside a
measured ownership region with a visible boundary, header, and ID. Theme owns
its presentation colors; color alone never establishes ownership. A reusable
Composite uses the same visible native expansion, because encapsulation limits
user access rather than evidence.

Layout measures native/operator blocks and complete child regions first. A
parent packs each child as one unit, never rewrites its internals, and attaches
connector structures only at authored endpoints and registered public anchors.
Independent peers follow declaration order or one complete explicit order.
Buses and links are conductive routing demands, not component slots or
pairwise-clique generators. Root Ports stay on their root buses, parent-owned
shunts stay in the parent region, and scopes containing only native peers remain
valid without an invented child or global neighbor partition.

The geometry uses the retained uniform `U = 2.2` metric, measured text bounds,
registered anchors, collision obstacles, continuous same-net wires, true T
junctions, and jump arcs only for different-net crossings. Name and value
labels remain separate and readable at the retained minimum scale. Ownership
regions, brackets, labels, and guides are visibly nonconductive.

The target does not promise a universal graph-layout algorithm. A failure names
the scope or declared constraints that could not be placed. It returns no
partial or best-effort certified diagram and does not invent retry, drawing-size,
threshold, or time knobs.

## Independent certification {#independent-certification}

One immutable diagram certificate carries expected and independently observed
evidence. The neutral scene cannot contain hidden answer tables that let a
witness copy the expected result.

### Electrical witness A

Witness A reconstructs visible component bodies, ordered terminals, wires,
junctions, grounds, Ports, couplings, and compiled matrix associations. For an
authoring projection it compares that reconstruction with the exact complete
Plan at the resolved effective parameter point. For a compiled projection it
compares with the exact compiler-emitted expansion for that same Plan and
point. Identity or correspondence mismatch fails.

When `show_parameter_values=True`, witness A also reconstructs every displayed
effective scalar physical value and its displayed unit, then compares both with
that same resolved point. When value labels are hidden, the scene makes no
visible-scalar-label claim, but the certificate still binds the exact effective
point. This presentation choice does not weaken the compiled projection's
required matrix, coefficient, sign, unit, half-shunt, or omission evidence.

This certifies projection correspondence only. It can detect a drawing or
projection-lowering mismatch, but it does not independently prove numerical
compiler lowering or stamping, a View/PTC realization, or solver correctness.
A correctly drawn yet numerically wrong compiler expansion can pass A/B;
Calculation validates compiler correctness separately. The observed witness
still reconstructs the visible evidence independently rather than copying an
expected manifest.

### Structural witness B

Witness B reconstructs visible:

- recursive Subsystem and Composite containment;
- series order and parallel branch membership;
- side-branch roles;
- bus and tap membership;
- complete N-link membership and public-boundary incidence;
- intrinsic, parent-applied, and Port-local ground presentation;
- public pin/coordinate/branch exposure; and
- nonconductive coupling relations.

Measured nonconductive operator brackets, short authored IDs, bus/tap marks,
exposure marks, ownership regions, and public boundary labels make those
relations observable where connectivity alone is ambiguous. Parallel branch
IDs survive a graphical permutation; witness B checks branch membership,
endpoints, and the ordered members inside each branch rather than demanding
declaration order equal geometric order. These marks annotate the one authored
circuit and never become a hidden answer table or second topology.

Witness B does not infer or certify the superseded S/P/M neighbor partition.
Every native leaf's complete occupied symbol-and-label geometry lies in its
owning region and outside child regions, except registered electrical crossings
at public boundary anchors.

### Human review C

Human review decides whether the explicit Plan is the intended circuit. A/B
correspondence, hashes, passing layout, and numerical execution cannot make
that design decision.

### Evidence table and digests

The review surface distinguishes observations from verified source facts. It
retains:

- Plan and catalog provenance;
- baseline and selected parameter values, Plan-specific physical consumers,
  and source units;
- Net/BOM and ordered pin/branch tables;
- expected and observed electrical and structural manifests;
- `plan_sha256`, `connectivity_sha256`, and `semantic_sha256`;
- compiler lineage and `expanded_graph_sha256` for compiled views; and
- optional `presentation_sha256` for the frozen scene.

Parameterized rendering additionally binds `parameters_sha256` for the
complete effective point after baseline filling. A selected point does not
mutate `plan_sha256`, but value-dependent expanded, omission, numerical, or
presentation identities may change. The expected witness and the observed A/B
reconstruction both use the same exact Plan and point.

Diagram-only grouping never removes an authored Link ID or its unordered
member set from structural evidence, and it never hides effective grounded-net
membership or the owner-local grounding role. Only the source-level batching
and tuple order of `ground_pins()` are nonsemantic provenance excluded from
physical and diagram digests.

The connectivity and semantic digests are representation-tagged. The Plan,
compiler-lineage, and expanded-graph identities retain their own existing
encoders. `expanded_graph_sha256` binds `plan_sha256`, `node_order`,
`resolved_bindings`, and `expanded_branch_rows`; it does not claim that every
solver stamp matrix is independently covered.

`presentation_sha256` excludes its own provenance annotation from the
canonical preimage. It is a reproducible presentation identity, not an
authenticity or security signature. Hiding provenance for publication changes
presentation only; the hidden band cannot be the sole code-free acceptance
packet.

## Compiled matrix-stamp projection {#compiled-projection}

A compiled transmission-line projection preserves the complete matrix-stamp
expansion rather than replacing it with a scalar-equivalent circuit. The
canonical equations, half-shunt handling, coefficient interpretation, and
required visible evidence remain in
[the compiled matrix-stamp implementation](../implementation/results-reports-and-diagrams.qmd#compiled-matrix-stamp-projection).
This contract owns only how that exact emitted expansion is projected and
independently checked for correspondence.

The compiler remains a trusted numerical baseline outside A/B correspondence.
A successful diagram audits its actual effective-point binding and visible
selected values. It does not prove compiler stamping or solver correctness,
unrelated calculation/request overrides, a View/PTC realization, or
optimization correctness.

## Result and presentation boundary {#diagram-result}

Successful rendering returns one immutable `CircuitDiagramResult`. Its
`show()` returns a real Schemdraw `Drawing` through the supported read-only
facade. The existing `Drawing.save()` remains the static-file API; this target
adds no second save/export surface.

Theme styling, Notebook zoom/pan/copy controls, and static fallback serialize
the same frozen checked scene. They cannot mutate it, invalidate the
certificate silently, or alter Plan, request, compiler, or Result identity.
Changing layout or Theme may change `presentation_sha256` while Plan,
connectivity, and semantic identities remain fixed for the same exact Plan,
complete effective parameter point, and representation. No invariance is
promised across changed parameter values.

Diagram rendering performs no simulation, allocates no `CircuitRun` workspace,
and creates no solver receipt. A screenshot or zero-output Notebook is
presentation, not certification or scientific evidence.

## Fail-closed behavior {#authoring-diagram-failures}

An individual authoring operation rejects violations knowable at that call,
including:

- a duplicate ID, a body already consumed by another structure, invalid
  operator cardinality, duplicate or coincident endpoints, or a redundant
  link;
- a foreign, private, or stale endpoint; a `CoordinateRef`, `PortRef`, or
  `GroundRef` used in a link; or a link that directly or transitively merges
  two same-scope buses;
- invalid `ground_pins()` cardinality, a non-pin/foreign/private pin, a
  duplicate logical pin, or an already-ground-equivalent pin;
- a duplicate tap ID, invalid public exposure, or more than one public pin for
  one internal node;
- a child Port, invalid Port role/load, implicit load/ground, invalid
  multi-terminal pair selection, or ineligible/unoriented/foreign mutual
  coupling.

Incomplete editable authoring is legal between calls. In particular, `add()`
does not fail merely because its new component has not yet been bound or given
a structural role. Complete-graph preflight at `CompositePlan.build()`,
immutable render capture, and `CircuitRun` seal instead rejects an unbound
terminal, an ordinary two-terminal native body outside exactly one structure,
a multiply consumed body, an incomplete independent Composite or multi-terminal
peer, an incomplete public map or exposure, an unrealizable mutual coupling, or
invalid final grounding and electrical closure.

These well-typed violations use
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="authoring")`, except ordinary Python signature
errors, wrong containers or endpoint types, and strict Enum/type violations
retain `TypeError`. Mutation of a sealed Plan retains `PlanSealedError`. A
failed operation rolls back that operation; a failed complete-graph preflight
leaves the prior graph editable and unsealed. Neither failure creates a partial
declaration or records the rejected attempt in diagnostic source history.

Rendering returns no `CircuitDiagramResult` when:

- a `SchematicLayout` contains missing, duplicate, foreign, dead, incomplete,
  or conflicting refs;
- required structures, labels, anchors, regions, or wires cannot be placed
  without collision or illegal crossing; or
- the selected deterministic local strategy produces no valid scene.

Those failures use `stage="schematic_layout"`. A mismatch between expected and
independently reconstructed electrical/structural evidence uses
`stage="schematic_audit"`. Neither creates a solver attempt, workspace,
receipt, or partial image.

## Tutorial realization {#tutorial-realization}

The canonical Tutorial files are QMD-first TARGET Chapter containers with
generated, zero-output Jupyter artifacts. Short Lessons inside a Chapter may
use its preceding state; every Chapter remains complete from a clean kernel.
They are syntax-valid documentation proposals, not runtime demonstrations:

Chapter 1 begins with a provisional expected-output/design-target sketch so the
learner knows what the authored model is meant to produce. It is not current
renderer output or certificate evidence. Runtime alignment must replace it
with a genuine Automatic Semantic Circuit Diagram Layout System (ASCDLS)
figure generated from the same fully assembled Plan and the existing
render/show/audit path, never with a separately maintained "correct circuit"
image.

| Chapter | Target authoring contribution |
|---|---|
| 1 | fixed-value inline grounded parallel LC, public pin, root coupling and Port, then diagram A/B/C review |
| 2–3 | the complete fixed-value declaration followed by Direct response and retained-node quantity questions |
| 4 | independent definitions, physical-field Plan binding, one selected point, and parameterized diagram evidence |
| 5 | Cartesian and listed parameter spaces, exact point outcomes, selection, and read-only collection |
| 6–7 | the complete parameterized declaration, optimization, report, and exact restart/resolve |
| 8 | project-owned Library |
| 9 | a complete reusable `CompositePlan` factory using the same structure grammar |
| 10 | that complete factory declaration and its public Composite boundary inside another Plan |
| 11 | automatic and handle-based hinted diagrams, one N-endpoint direct stitch, and parent-applied grounding |
| 12 | complete N=2 matrix line, named-tap N=1 feedline, then one whole-RLGC selected-point compiled diagram |
| 13 | one complete Chapter-local parameter-bound feedline/readout/floating capstone, its Plan diagram, then explicit probe PTC |
| 14 | the complete model followed by PTC, pair transform, and retain using public handles |
| 15 | the complete model followed by pump-off HB execution and exact restart/resolve routes |
| 16 | the complete model followed by independent-grid Direct/HB presentation |

Every Chapter is self-contained: it repeats all imports, physical declarations,
and direct handles needed to follow that Chapter from a fresh kernel. Its short
Lessons may share state in order, but no Chapter depends on an included builder,
a Python fixture, or state from another Notebook. This deliberate teaching
repetition does not duplicate contract authority; the declarations apply this
one target grammar.

Across the course, short TARGET cases distinguish intrinsic grounding,
parent-applied grounding, and Port loads; show two independent public returns
grounded to the one reference; and make rejected hierarchy, transitive-bus,
terminal-short, and grounded-Port attempts visible. A caught
authoring failure is followed by a corrected declaration that reuses the
rejected ID, demonstrating atomic failure rather than a partially mutated Plan.

The course always completes the authored model before choosing an analysis
question. ASCDLS translates the explicit Plan into an authoring or compiled
diagram and independently audits that projection. `CircuitRun` separately
supplies `run.original` and any selected analysis View. Rendering may project
one explicit parameter point, but it neither creates nor displays PTC,
transformed/retained coordinates, a parameter space, solver state, or an
analysis `Result`. Successful audited rendering returns the
`CircuitDiagramResult` defined above.

The historical dev5/dev6 numerical meanings remain intact in their renumbered
Chapters 12–16.
No current fixture, source file, test, or runtime implementation is evidence
that the target grammar already executes.

## Honest limits and supersession {#honest-limits}

- This document is a `CONVERGING` target, not Human acceptance, stabilization,
  integration, release, or scientific-result evidence.
- Implementation alignment remains pending. Durable tests wait for later Human
  acceptance of an exact implementation candidate.
- The frozen implementation may still contain `net()`, `ground(*pins)`, legacy
  diagram classes, or a catalog-hint candidate. Those bytes are interpretation
  evidence only and do not compete with this target authority.
- This target has no public generic netlist-to-intent inference, no
  `SchematicCatalog`, no Participant/Interface/Attachment refs, no S/P/M
  relation API, and no raw coordinate override.
- It does not promise automatic layout for every circuit, infer physical flow,
  or turn diagram success into a product/scientific Gate.
- It does not certify a consumer Design Target, measurement, solver accuracy,
  optimization, PTC, transformed View, or Human intent.
